conventions.convention: The Minkowski signature is (-+++), x⁰ = ct is a length coordinate, μ ≥ 0 has inverse-length units, and the shell phase is p ∘ x = ωμ x⁰ − k · x.
Free-field Hilbert pairings are linear in the second variable; creation is linear and annihilation conjugate-linear in the one-particle argument.
The scalar shell measure is d³k/((2π)³2ωμ), with the massless apex omitted. Kμf(p) = ∫f(x)exp(ip ∘ x)d⁴x has no Fourier prefactor.
Countable Choice is assumed: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function.

The scalar field is √2 times the Segal field, and its Weyl operator is WSegal(√2Kμf). Local scalar observables form the unital operator-norm-closed Weyl algebra; local Dirac observables form the norm closure of even products of bounded smeared fields and adjoints.

Physical scalar momentum is ℏdΓ(kj), whereas the cited mathematical scalar spatial translation generator is dΓ(−kj). Physical Hamiltonians multiply the inverse-length generators by ℏc; these nonzero scalings and signs leave their domains unchanged.
The classical Dirac components commute, γ⁰ = β, γʲ = βαʲ, and {γᵃ,γᵇ} = −2ηᵃᵇI. Actions are used through compactly supported variations, without assuming convergence of their global integrals.

Point-smearing widths are positive lengths; profiles are nonnegative normalized Schwartz functions of dimensionless coordinates. The scalar obstruction concerns vacuum-vector norm, and the equal-time Dirac obstruction concerns operator norm.

Species/statistics assignments and vacua are adopted physical assumptions. Born probabilities require a supplied density state and normalized finite bounded Kraus instrument; none of these items reports observations.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice, μ ≥ 0, and the selected free-field model. Real scalar smearings have self-adjoint closures on their exact Segal domains; the listed scalar and Dirac generators have maximal sector-sum domains. Normalized vectors in D(A) have finite mean and variance, without requiring D(A²); AB requires membership in D(B) and BΨ ∈ D(A). Scalar Weyl algebras and even Dirac algebras commute across open spacelike-separated regions. For every normalized nonnegative Schwartz spacetime profile rescaled about x₀, the scalar vacuum-vector norms diverge as the width tends to zero; the stated normalized spatial spinor profiles similarly have diverging equal-time Dirac operator norms. The construction supplies no point fields or coincident products, and asserts no empirical outcome.

Under Countable Choice and the selected free-field model, smooth real scalar and smooth commuting Dirac classical fields have compact-variation stationarity equations (□ − μ²)φn = 0 and (iγᵃ∂a − μ)ψn = 0. The separately adopted representations satisfy Φμ((□ − μ²)f) = 0 and Ψ((i∂₀ − hD(−i∇))F) = 0 for the stated Schwartz tests. The differential expressions agree in the declared conventions; the representations, species/statistics assignments and vacua are additional assumptions, not deductions from the actions.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit foundational assumption carried by both physics theorems and inherited by the Gaussian counterexample.

Sequence-indexed convergence of normalized Schwartz point smearings, convergence of their Fourier profiles at zero, and convergence on finite shell annuli. Each application supplies an integrable majorant; arbitrary width sequences establish the full width limit.

concerns.concern: The Statement says, “For each fixed coordinate time t in seconds,” while using Ψ_t(u) exactly as defined in lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality. That supplier uses W_D(t,k), and def-qft-dirac-projections explicitly defines t as a length-coordinate increment in cos(ωt) and sin(ωt). With ω in inverse metres, substituting a seconds-valued t is dimensionally inconsistent. The physical-time version needs the explicit reparameterization Ψ_phys,t(u) := Ψ_ct(u), or the parameter should retain its length-coordinate units. The CAR norm-divergence argument survives either clarification.

seams_checked.note: The consumer preserves the specified scalar bosonic and Dirac CAR adoption, selected vacua, bounded observable definitions, physical momentum normalization, and conditional measurement interpretation. It does not derive statistics or empirical validity from the classical actions.

The compact-variation stationarity iff equations, maximal operator domains, finite variance on D(A), and composition-domain restrictions match the inspected suppliers. The consumer's scalar point-smearing proof independently establishes its arbitrary normalized nonnegative Schwartz-profile scope. No time-ordered-kernel conclusion is imported.

The shell measure, Fourier phase, √2 Segal normalization, Klein–Gordon test annihilation, and bounded Weyl locality agree with the supplier statements. The sign conversion □ − μ² = −(∂₀² − Δ + μ²) is explicit; the massless apex causes no divergence at the lower integration endpoint.

The bounded CAR, even-algebra locality, tested Hamiltonian-form Dirac equation and maximal generator domains are faithfully used. However, the equal-time field parameter is relabelled as seconds although its supplier defines a length-coordinate parameter; see the concern on pthm-qft-free-observable-domain-limits.
